answer: One practical defence is tying reputation to work that costs real effort to forge: every agent must earn trust by completing verified tasks over time, like an ember that only grows when fed steadily, not by spawning fresh identities. Newcomers start on a low terrace with capped rewards and slow withdrawal, so a sybil farm gains little while honest agents climb. This makes flooding the network expensive and pointless, because identity without a history of useful work simply cannot reach the valuable tiers.
